title: Numerical first-cohomology estimate for a coherent free quotient
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $n\geq1$, $r\geq1$, and $b\geq1$ an integer, and put $X=\mathbf P^n_k$. Let
$$0\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow\mathcal O_X^{\oplus r}\longrightarrow F\longrightarrow0$$
be a short exact sequence of coherent modules [pqf-def-coherent]. Use twists $E(d)=E\otimes\mathcal O_X(d)$ [def-pc-projective-space-twist], module sheaf cohomology [pqf-def-cohomology], Euler characteristics [def-pc-euler-characteristic] and finite vector-space dimensions [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. Assume $H^q(X,K(b))=0$ for every $q\geq2$, and put $C=\binom{n+b}{n}$. Then
$$\chi(X,K(b))=rC-\chi(X,F(b)),\qquad \dim_kH^0(X,K(b))\leq rC,$$
and
$$0\leq\dim_kH^1(X,K(b))=\dim_kH^0(X,K(b))-\chi(X,K(b))\leq\chi(X,F(b)).$$
In particular, for every polynomial $P\in\mathbf Q[t]$ with $\chi(X,F(d))=P(d)$ for every integer $d$, one has
$$0\leq\dim_kH^1(X,K(b))\leq P(b)\leq\max(0,\lceil P(b)\rceil).$$

source.place: Tag 08AG (lemma-bound-quotients-free), final paragraph starting On the other hand, by the vanishing of the higher cohomology groups; the numerical estimate is stated at b >= 1 to avoid the erroneous assertion about H0 at twist zero.

proof.text: Put $L=\mathcal O_X(b)$. By the twist definition $L$ is locally free of rank one, so tensor exactness and tensor symmetry give an exact sequence with middle term $\mathcal O_X^{\oplus r}\otimes L$. Identify this term with $L^{\oplus r}$ by $(a_i)_i\otimes s\mapsto(a_i s)_i$; the inverse sends $(s_i)_i$ to $\sum_i e_i\otimes s_i$, where $e_i$ are the standard basis sections. These maps are inverse by bilinearity and commute with restriction, giving $0\to K(b)\to L^{\oplus r}\to F(b)\to0$. These twists are coherent by the defining local conditions for coherence: on each trivializing open, tensoring identifies the twisted module with the original one, so finite generation and finite generation of kernels of maps from finite free modules hold on the same neighbourhoods. These local conditions give coherence on X. Projective-space properness applies to the finite coordinate set $\{0,\ldots,n\}$ over $\operatorname{Spec}k$. The proper coherent cohomology theorem therefore gives finite-dimensional cohomology and well-defined Euler characteristics for all three terms.

source.place: Tag 08AG, lemma-bound-quotients-free, final numerical paragraph (at positive twist b)

proof.text: For $0\leq j\leq r$, $L^{\oplus j}$ is coherent directly from the coherence definition: the projection from the coherent $L^{\oplus r}$ gives finite type, and a map from a finite free module into $L^{\oplus j}$ has the same kernel after composing with its split inclusion into $L^{\oplus r}$. In particular, $L$ is coherent because $r\ge1$. Apply projective twist cohomology with $A=k$ and $d=b\ge1$: $H^0(X,L)$ has basis the monomials $x_0^{e_0}\cdots x_n^{e_n}$ with nonnegative exponents summing to $b$, and all positive cohomology vanishes. There are $C=\binom{b+n}{n}$ such monomials: write $b$ identical marks separated into $n+1$ consecutive blocks by $n$ separators, and choose the separator positions among the $b+n$ positions. Thus $\dim H^0(X,L)=\chi(X,L)=C$, with the Euler sum justified by coherence and properness. A section of the finite direct sum $L^{\oplus r}$ is an $r$-tuple of sections. For each monomial basis section $m$ and each index $1\le i\le r$, place $m$ in coordinate $i$ and zero elsewhere. These $rC$ tuples span by expanding each coordinate in the monomial basis; a relation is zero only when every coefficient is zero, by independence in each coordinate. They are therefore a basis, so the section space has dimension $rC$. For $0\le j<r$, Euler additivity for $0\to L^{\oplus j}\to L^{\oplus(j+1)}\to L\to0$ gives $\chi(X,L^{\oplus(j+1)})=\chi(X,L^{\oplus j})+C$. The zero sheaf has zero cohomology and Euler characteristic, so induction starting at $j=0$ proves $\chi(X,L^{\oplus j})=jC$ for every $j\le r$, in particular the required equality at $j=r$.

source.place: Tag 08AG, lemma-bound-quotients-free, final numerical paragraph (at positive twist b)

proof.text: Euler additivity applied to the twisted sequence gives $\chi(X,K(b))=rC-\chi(X,F(b))$. The cohomology sequence begins with an injection $H^0(X,K(b))\hookrightarrow H^0(X,L^{\oplus r})$. Hence $h^0(K(b))\le rC$: the image of a basis under an injective linear map is linearly independent in the target, whose dimension is $rC$.

source.place: Tag 08AG, lemma-bound-quotients-free, final numerical paragraph (at positive twist b)

proof.text: In the finite Euler sum for $K(b)$, every term of degree $q\ge2$ is zero by the hypothesis. Therefore $\chi(X,K(b))=h^0(K(b))-h^1(K(b))$. Rearranging and substituting step 3 gives $h^1(K(b))=h^0(K(b))-rC+\chi(X,F(b))\le\chi(X,F(b))$. Dimensions are nonnegative integers, proving the full asserted chain.

source.place: Tag 08AG, lemma-bound-quotients-free, final numerical paragraph (at positive twist b)

proof.text: For the asserted polynomial $P$, substitute $\chi(X,F(b))=P(b)$. The preceding inequality also proves $P(b)\ge0$. By the defining property of the ceiling, $P(b)\le\lceil P(b)\rceil$, and this is at most $\max(0,\lceil P(b)\rceil)$. This proves the final chain.
